p.title: Handling prejudice
p.challenge: Two hostels are hostile. Sort each idea: will it reduce prejudice or not?

items.text: Both hostels work together to build the college stage
Mixed teams for a cooperative project
items.why: Intergroup contact in a cooperative context.

items.text: Talks that correct stereotypes about each hostel
Getting to know students as individuals
A fierce hostel-vs-hostel competition
items.why: Contact in a competitive context can increase hostility.

items.text: Contact where seniors of one hostel order juniors of the other
items.why: Contact works best with equal status.

items.text: Stressing "our hostel is the best" in every event

p.title: Group, team, crowd or audience?
p.challenge: Sort each collection of people

items.text: A family that cooks and eats together
items.why: Interdependent, with roles and norms: a group.

items.text: A school eco-club with rules and members
items.why: Common goals, roles and norms: a group.

items.text: Quiz team: a history, a science and a sports expert
items.why: Complementary skills, mutual accountability: a team.

items.text: A surgical team in an operation theatre
items.why: Complementary skills, common goal: a team.

items.text: People gathered after a minor road accident
items.why: Present by chance, no structure: a crowd.

items.text: Shoppers in a busy market
items.why: No belongingness or interdependence: a crowd.

items.text: Viewers at a cinema hall
items.why: Gathered for a special purpose, generally passive: an audience.
